newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs languish on low end of range.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs languish on low end of range.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures spent Tuesday languishing on the lower end of their recent trading range as the previous day's rally in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ran out of steam, dealers said.
"The market is pretty sedate at the moment. If the Euroyen rallies four or five ticks, people sell it," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
"The interest rate has gone down to its lowest already. I don't think they'll cut it any more unless there are more problems in the financial sector," he added.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.33 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.35. December, which became the benchmark contract in Tokyo on Thursday, was at 99.21 against 99.22.
Turnover for the December contract exceeded September by 485 lots on SIMEX.
March JGBs settled at 126.34 against their previous 126.65.
Dealers said the Nikkei's strong rebound also weighed on both ends of the Japanese yield curve on Thursday.
Eurodollar futures finished little changed as players adjusted their positions ahead of the closely-watched U.S. Employment Cost Index for the fourth quarter, due to be released at 1330 GMT.

Consensus estimates point to a 0.9 percent increase but a number above 1.0 percent could spark a strong sell-off in treasuries as it would spark fears of a rate hike by the Federal Reserve as early as its February meeting.
September Eurodollars ended at 93.96 against their IMM close at 93.95.
